gate: A rusted portcullis hangs a hand above the floor and you heave it up on your back.
You put your shoulder to a door swollen shut with brine and force the wood to give.
A fallen beam pins the only lantern and you lift it until the light breathes again.
The chain across the stair is old and thick and you wrench a link until it parts.
Black water pours through a split in the wall and you hold a slab against the flood.
You haul a drowned bell up from the cistern by its rope until it clears the water.
A wall of packed bone blocks the passage and you break through it with your fists.
The door is iron and the lock is rust and you bend the bar until the bolt snaps.
A sunk barge lists across the channel and you shove its rotten hull aside.
The gate wheel has seized with salt and you turn it a full round on your own.
The stair weeps salt and you carry a fallen friend up every step of it.
A cold current drags at your legs and you wade the flooded hall against it.
Roots thick as anchor rope have knotted over the arch and you tear them down.
The choir stone has slid across the well mouth and you roll it back to the wall.
A stone lid seals the ossuary and you lift it clear with both arms.
Ice has sealed the sluice and you drive your heel through it until the water runs.
You hold the sagging lintel on your shoulders while the others crawl beneath.
A drowned tree lies across the causeway and you drag it, trunk and all, into the dark.
You stand chest deep in the black cistern and endure the cold until the lock turns.
A capstan is seized solid with rust and you walk its bar around alone.
You lift the grating off the drain and hold it while the black water chokes through.
A stone coffin blocks the stair and you tip it over the edge into the dark.
The hatch is rusted into its frame and you tear it up by the ring.
You break the ice skin on the cistern with your elbow and climb down into it.
A drowned mast leans over the path and you push it back until it falls the other way.
You drag the sunk lord's anchor off the trapdoor one link at a time.
The bone gate is barred with a thigh bone and you snap it across your knee.
You shove a cart of salt blocks up the ramp before it rolls back onto the others.
A slab of the ceiling has come down on the path and you prop it high enough to crawl.
You wrestle the ferry pole out of the mud where the last boatman left it.
The door of the drowned forge is jammed and you kick it in.
You carry the cracked bell on your back across the flooded nave.
Barnacles have welded the hatch shut and you beat them off with a rock.
You pull a sleeping keeper's chair out of the doorway with the keeper still in it.
The rope ladder is soaked to lead and you haul it up the shaft alone.
You break the rusted hinges off the ossuary door and lift the door aside.
A whale jaw has fallen across the tunnel and you lever it up on a spar.
The sluice paddle has jammed half open and you force it down against the current.
You drive an iron spike into the seam of the wall and climb the crack it opens.
A heap of drowned nets fills the arch and you rip a way through with your hands.
chain: You pump a stiff handle until the well runs dry, then hold it down as the water climbs.
You work a rusted bellows until the coals redden, then work on until the iron glows.
You draw a raft over deep water on a wet hawser, and draw it back with them aboard.
You dig the muck from a choked drain, then shoulder the bank back when it slides in.
You bail a leaking hull until the water thins, then stuff the seams while it weeps.
You bear a climber on a wet line while their boots slip, then bring them over the ledge.
You prise a buried anchor out of the silt, then walk it clear of the shallows.
You sink a wedge under the settling floor, then drive a second when the first splits.
You lift the drowned door off its pins, then carry it to bridge the gap.
You break the ice at the well mouth, then haul the bucket up through the slush.
You drag the fallen spar aside, then brace it under the sagging roof.
You turn the rusted capstan a quarter, then hold it while the chain catches.
You shoulder the barrow up the salt ramp, then keep it from rolling back down.
You pull the stuck oar free of the mud, then row against the current to the stair.
You wrench the grate loose, then lower yourself through into the flooded cellar.
You pry the lid off the cistern, then wade in to your waist to find the valve.
You split the swollen door with your shoulder, then pull the halves apart.
You beat the rust off the chain links, then drag the chain through the pulley.
You roll the stone from the tunnel mouth, then wedge it so it cannot roll back.
You break the bone bar across the gate, then force the gate against the silt.
You drag the dead eel off the channel grate, then lift the grate out of the water.
You tear the net from the arch, then cut the knots that still hold the far side.
You kick the rotten hatch in, then catch the ladder before it falls into the hold.
You push the sunk cart off the rails, then walk it to the edge of the pit.
You drag the capsized skiff up the shingle, then flip it over to shelter the lantern.
You drag the anchor chain up the shore, then loop it round the rock to hold the boat.
You break the seal on the flood door, then brace against the water that follows.
You haul the rope bridge taut, then tie it off before the knot can slip.
You wade out to the stranded skiff, then push it back against the tide.
You lift the stone font out of the doorway, then set it down without cracking it.
You tip the flooded boat on its side, then hold it up while the water runs out.
You carry the salt barrels up the stair, then stack them against the flooding door.
You wrestle the drowned statue off its plinth, then stand it on the trapdoor.
You break the iced chain from the post, then haul the gate up on it hand over hand.
You drag the coffin lid half across, then climb inside to reach the hidden stair.
You heave on the jammed sluice wheel, then keep heaving when it slips back a turn.
You pull the keel beam out of the silt, then use it to ram the barred door.
You snap the frozen mooring rope, then pull the barge in by its bow ring.
You hoist the lantern cage to the hook, then hold the rope while it swings.
You bend two bars of the cage apart, then hold them while you climb out.
